past_medical_history: Remote ischemic stroke (left MCA territory, 5 years ago, with mild residual right hand weakness)

patient.chief_complaint: Worsening walking difficulties and cognitive decline on top of prior stroke — admitted for NPH evaluation
patient.history_present_illness: A 72-year-old right-handed Hispanic man with hypertension, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on apixaban, and a remote left MCA ischemic stroke 5 years ago (with mild residual right hand weakness that has been stable since 6 months post-stroke) was admitted for NPH evaluation. He and his son report that over approximately 10-12 months, he has developed new symptoms on top of his post-stroke baseline: his gait, which had been stable at his post-stroke level for years, has significantly worsened with shuffling quality, wide base, and difficulty initiating movement. He has had two falls at home in the past 4 months. His son notes he is far more forgetful and slowed in thinking than he was 18 months ago. He now needs assistance managing his medications. Additionally, he has developed urinary urgency with two episodes of incontinence per week. His outpatient neurologist initially attributed the gait decline to evolving small vessel disease from his prior stroke history, but repeat MRI showed ventriculomegaly with Evans index 0.34 out of proportion to cortical atrophy, and he was referred for NPH evaluation. The challenge in this case is that the remote stroke and ongoing small vessel disease create significant diagnostic complexity — distinguishing NPH from progressive post-stroke vascular changes.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x3. MoCA 20/30. Mild right upper extremity weakness (4+/5) unchanged from post-stroke baseline. Speech slightly dysarthric (chronic, post-stroke). Memory: delayed recall 2/5. Executive function moderately impaired on trail-making.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal, 3mm, reactive. Right lower facial droop (chronic). Tongue deviates mildly right (chronic).
neurological_exam.motor: Right hand weakness 4+/5 (chronic post-stroke). Left side 5/5. Increased tone bilateral lower extremities — mild spasticity in right leg (post-stroke) and rigidity-like increased tone bilateral lower extremities (possible NPH component). No new focal deficits.
neurological_exam.sensory: Mild right hemibody sensory loss to light touch (chronic). Vibration reduced at toes bilaterally.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Brisk right upper and lower extremity (2+/3+) chronic. Left side 2+. Right Babinski (chronic post-stroke).
neurological_exam.coordination: Right finger-nose mildly clumsy (chronic). Left finger-nose intact.
neurological_exam.gait: Wide-based, shuffling. Short steps. Right leg mild circumduction (post-stroke). TUG 32 seconds. 10-meter walk 26 seconds. Gait significantly worse than 12 months ago per son.

signal_characteristics.description: Chronic encephalomalacia with gliosis in left temporal and inferior parietal region
Tight sulci at high vertex with widening of sylvian fissures
Callosal angle 82 degrees on coronal imaging

mri.impression: Evans index 0.34 (exceeds 0.3 NPH criterion). Callosal angle 82 degrees (meets <90 degree criterion). DESH pattern partially present. Chronic left MCA territory infarct stable. Significant white matter disease. The concurrent chronic stroke and severe white matter disease are significant confounders for NPH diagnosis. High-volume tap trial and careful gait analysis are required. Clinical correlation recommended.

abnormal_values_summary: Apixaban anti-Xa slightly elevated at trough (0.18 IU/mL) — hold 24h before LP

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 15 cmH2O. WBC: 2 cells/mcL (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 52 mg/dL. Glucose: 66 mg/dL (ratio 0.69). cytology: No malignant cells. beta_amyloid_42: 742 pg/mL (normal). total_tau: 196 pg/mL (normal). phospho_tau: 31 pg/mL (normal).

specialized_test.test_type: High-volume tap trial (40 mL) with quantitative gait analysis

findings.gait_description: Post-tap: marginally improved step height and length; less initiation difficulty; right circumduction gait unchanged (post-stroke component)

specialized_test.impression: Tap trial shows borderline improvement (17% TUG, 19% 10m walk) — below the 20% threshold for positive tap trial. Cognitive testing unchanged. This is an equivocal-negative tap trial in the context of Evans index 0.34 and callosal angle 82 degrees. The chronic stroke makes interpretation of gait changes difficult. Extended lumbar drainage trial is recommended to improve predictive accuracy.
recommended_actions: Extended lumbar drainage trial to better characterize tap trial response
Neurosurgery consultation regardless — imaging criteria support NPH

findings.cognitive: MoCA 22/30 at end of drainage (2 points improvement)

output.impression: Extended drainage trial shows progressive gait improvement to 28% over 72 hours, exceeding the 20% threshold that single tap trial did not reach. Progressive improvement over days (rather than immediate) is characteristic of NPH response. This confirms NPH diagnosis and supports VP shunting.
recommended_actions: VP shunt with pressure-adjustable valve recommended

output.impression: Significantly hyperdynamic aqueductal CSF flow (peak velocity 24 cm/s, stroke volume 88 mcL/cycle) — both well above threshold. Strongly supports NPH pathophysiology. This confirms NPH diagnosis despite the equivocal single tap trial.
recommended_actions: VP shunt strongly supported by hyperdynamic CSF flow

findings.result: Moderately impaired — both encoding and retrieval
Mildly impaired — mild aphasia consistent with chronic left temporal stroke

quantitative_data.profile: Mixed: left hemisphere cognitive deficits from stroke + frontal-subcortical profile consistent with NPH

output.impression: Complex neuropsychological profile reflecting two concurrent conditions: chronic left MCA stroke (mild aphasia, right-sided motor/sensory deficits) superimposed on frontal-subcortical cognitive syndrome consistent with NPH. The frontal-subcortical component (executive dysfunction, severe processing speed impairment) is likely to benefit from shunting.
recommended_actions: VP shunting expected to improve NPH-related frontal-subcortical component

findings.finding: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity with involuntary contractions at 120 mL fill

output.impression: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity (NDO) consistent with NPH-related frontal lobe dysfunction. Pattern distinct from prior stroke-related NDO — would benefit from shunting.
recommended_actions: Low-dose tolterodine for symptomatic relief pre-shunt

output.impression: Negative amyloid PET. No significant cortical amyloid accumulation. Alzheimer's co-pathology not supported. Shunt prognosis favorable from amyloid standpoint.

output.proposed: VP shunt surgery with apixaban management
interactions: Apixaban must be held 48h prior to neurosurgical procedure with bleeding risk
warnings: Discuss with neurosurgery and hematology regarding bridging anticoagulation for AF during perioperative apixaban hold
Resume apixaban 24-48h post-operatively once hemostasis confirmed
Stroke risk during apixaban hold must be weighed against bleeding risk of shunt surgery

differential.diagnosis: Progressive vascular dementia from small vessel disease and prior stroke
differential.key_features: Significant WMH, prior stroke, hypertension — but ventriculomegaly with Evans 0.34, callosal angle 82 degrees, and eventual positive extended drainage trial support NPH
Gait disorder — but no tremor, no cogwheel rigidity, ventriculomegaly present
Prior MCA stroke — but new gait changes, ventriculomegaly, and incontinence onset are new from 12 months ago and distinct from post-stroke baseline

optimal_actions.action: Review brain MRI — Evans index, callosal angle, white matter disease
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Evans 0.34, callosal angle 82, severe WMH, chronic stroke
Normal labs; apixaban level mildly elevated — hold 24h before LP

optimal_actions.action: High-volume tap trial after holding apixaban 24h
Extended 72h lumbar drainage trial (single tap trial equivocal-negative)

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Surgical treatment with careful anticoagulation management

critical_actions: Hold apixaban 24-48h before lumbar puncture to minimize hemorrhagic complications
Extended lumbar drainage trial is indicated when single tap trial is equivocal-negative with positive imaging criteria
Discuss anticoagulation bridging strategy perioperatively with neurosurgery and hematology
Do not attribute new gait decline solely to prior stroke — baseline was stable for years
contraindicated_actions: Performing lumbar puncture without checking and managing anticoagulation status
Attributing all gait decline to chronic stroke without investigating NPH given new ventriculomegaly
Withholding shunt without attempting extended drainage trial when single tap trial is equivocal
key_reasoning_points: The moderate-difficulty element is the complex background of prior stroke and severe white matter disease making NPH diagnosis challenging
Anticoagulation management is a critical safety issue for lumbar puncture and VP shunt surgery
Extended drainage trial overcomes the limitation of equivocal single tap trial and confirms NPH
Hyperdynamic CSF flow on PC-MRI provides objective evidence supporting NPH diagnosis independent of tap trial response
Negative amyloid PET improves shunt prognosis

red_herrings.data_point: Chronic left MCA stroke with residual right hand weakness and gait changes
red_herrings.intended_effect: New gait decline attributed to progressive post-stroke changes rather than new NPH
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Post-stroke baseline was stable for years; new shuffling wide-based gait (distinct from post-stroke circumduction) with ventriculomegaly Evans 0.34 represents superimposed NPH

metadata.difficulty_variant_description: Moderate NPH with prior ischemic stroke creating diagnostic complexity; anticoagulation management required for LP; single tap trial equivocal-negative but extended drainage confirms diagnosis.
